title: Pearl FP8 certificate-v4 verifier parity and claim-boundary gate
question: Can two independent implementations reproduce the proposed certificate-v4 selected-tile verifier and Blackwell/B200 arithmetic on frozen vectors, reject preregistered degenerate cases, and preserve the boundary between Pearl WORK and Aeye EXECUTION?

frozen_inputs.value: Blackwell SM100 / B200 as declared by the retained proposal

procedure: Translate the retained specification into an explicit relation manifest covering Device, Quant, dimensions, periodic partitions, commitments, selected tile, ticket, and jackpot-policy checks; retain every ambiguity instead of resolving it by convention.
Audit the retained PR patch against that manifest and classify each difference as implementation detail, specification gap, contradiction, or unknown; do not treat the open PR as activated consensus.

Construct immutable ordinary, boundary, and adversarial vectors for post-noise quantization, selected-tile multiplication, correction, transcript hashing, and jackpot checks in two implementations that do not share parser or arithmetic code.
Cross-check the declared bit-exact arithmetic against retained vectors from an authorized target B200 path; a CPU emulator may be one implementation but cannot certify its own physical fidelity.

Measure native tile work, quantization, noise generation, hashing, commitment construction/verification, memory movement, and verifier work separately; keep the specification's MAC work model distinct from end-to-end cost.
Emit only a certificate-v4 WORK/profile result. Do not infer request, model-graph, full execution, output, hardware origin, or demand.
acceptance: The specification-to-code map has no unresolved consensus-critical parser, quantization, arithmetic, commitment, ticket, or jackpot ambiguity for the tested profile.
Two independent implementations agree byte-for-byte on every accepted vector and reject every known-bad vector for the preregistered reason.
The independent arithmetic result agrees with retained authorized B200 outputs for all ordinary, boundary, and adversarial cases.
The report preserves quantized-subspace hardness as a declared non-standard assumption and reports its scope rather than assigning a numeric security level.
The result is reported only as proposed certificate-v4 WORK verification and bounded arithmetic conformance, never as Aeye EXECUTION or useful demand.
failure: Any unresolved divergence between the specification and retained implementation blocks a general certificate-v4 verifier claim.
Any vector disagreement is retained and classified; parameters may not be adjusted after observing the target output.
Absence of independent B200 outputs blocks physical arithmetic-conformance acceptance even if two software implementations agree.
A security conclusion derived from average-case vectors without a formal assumption or adversarial analysis is unsupported.
Any attempt to reuse certificate-v3 INT vectors, parser rules, or hardness identifiers fails the version firewall.
known_bad_controls: Change one Device or Quant parameter while retaining all other bytes; the relation identifier or verification result must change.
Change one operand commitment or disclosed strip after the ticket is fixed; authentication must fail.
Use zero/no-noise or below-floor noise where the jackpot policy forbids it; the policy check must reject.
Use a tamed or low-unpredictability product outside the accepted bounds; the policy check must reject.
Truncate, round, or accumulate under a non-B200 arithmetic profile while preserving the profile label; conformance must fail.
Attach a valid certificate-v4 WORK object to an execution proof with a different operand root; the Aeye cross-evidence validator must reject.
blocking_conditions: No immutable certificate-v4 reference-vector suite is retained.
No authorized Blackwell/B200 execution path and independent captured vectors are identified.
No second parser/arithmetic implementation independent of the retained PR exists in Aeye.
The retained PR was open and unmerged at retrieval, so activation and final consensus rules are unknown.
Operator acceptance of this proposed experiment manifest has not been recorded.
